purpose: Candidate finite-model cuts and future isolated observation protocol, not a runner or product test.
execution_scope: Read-only source research; no imports of product code, no kill/restart/power experiments, no business writes.

application_volatile: Store instance state and Promise queue
DSH Session live log/inbox and JSONL buffered batch
os_visible: Formal projects.json pathname and content visible through OS
Host log bytes visible to local reads
stable_storage: Only the prefixes/names guaranteed by a frozen OS/filesystem/device durability profile
model_axes.historical_receipt: An immutable receipt from an earlier command; not a current grant or a fresh send permission.

profile_parameters_to_freeze: single Store instance versus multiple writers
target active JSONL writer and live-event routing
failure at target drain versus unrelated handle versus rollback failure
later successful drain allowed before crash
meaning of API acknowledgment and replay receipt
finite transition bound or future observation window

obligations.description: One authoritative writer or conflict detection, with read-check-write and idempotency checks in the actual serialized boundary.
Define durability level and atomic relationship of authoritative state, outbound intent and request identity/receipt; baseline Store only couples projects/outbox.
Retain send intent, stable action/message identity and current admission conditions across crash; local commit is not remote submission.
Distinguish live ID presence from durable recipient acceptance; failed writes and retries retain responsibility for the durability barrier.
Distinguish target receipt, unrelated flush failure, local sent-marker failure and actual business effect; errors do not prove absence.
Restore exact command identities from durable authoritative journal and treat repeated receipts as historical, never as renewed authorization.

classification.SUCCESS: Frozen profile's applicable property is supported by declared observations; safe refusal may pass a contract but is not business completion.
classification.FAILURE: An explicit tested property is contradicted by an observable trace under its declared assumptions; a model counterexample is not proof of an incident.
classification.UNSUPPORTED: Required capability/profile/probe is absent or the trace violates a stated precondition, so that product assurance cannot be evaluated.
classification.UNKNOWN: Evidence cannot distinguish commit/no-commit or target/other failure within the frozen observation scope.
classification.NOT_RUN: Current value for every cut; neither model enumeration nor product fault injection was executed in this line.

cuts.title: 临时文件、替换、内存发布与回执的崩溃切点
initial_state: Choose existing valid main file S0 or initially absent file as separate variants.
One Store writer, no concurrent mutations; next state S1 contains both project delta and outbox intent.
cut_points: After callback, before temporary write completes
After writeFile resolves, before rename
After rename resolves, before this.state assignment
After this.state publication, before caller receives result
After caller receives result, before an unproven stable-storage boundary
cuts.perturbation: A future model may drop only the layers specified by process-crash or power-failure profile; no crash is performed here.
observables: presence of temporary file as diagnostic only

success: Under local atomic-rename and process-only failure assumptions, no partial new JSON is exposed as the authoritative main file by the replacement sequence.
If durable completion is claimed, acknowledgment follows the profile's required data and namespace barriers.
failure: An acknowledged durability guarantee is contradicted by recovery under the same frozen guarantee.
State and intent recover from different versions despite a claimed atomic pair.
unsupported: No defined power-failure contract: a process-restart observation cannot evaluate power-loss durability.
unknown: Ambiguous rename/write error, missing authoritative path without commit evidence, or unfixed filesystem semantics.

cuts.baseline_static_prediction: Single Store stages both state and intent together, but has no explicit sync step. This is absence of a demonstrated power-loss guarantee, not evidence that data has actually been lost.

cuts.title: 两个 Store 与外层判重的交错
initial_state: Variant A: two Store instances independently open the same S0; they may be in one process or different processes.
Variant B: one Store, two concurrent Projects.dispatch calls with the same dispatch key both read the pre-change project.
cut_points: A and B both read S0 before either replacement
Writer A replaces S0 with S0+a and receives success; writer B later replaces with S0+b
Both duplicate-key checks return absent before queued push callbacks run
cuts.perturbation: Enumerate these interleavings in a future model only.
observables: dispatch key and generated thread IDs
presence or absence of an enforced single-writer/CAS rejection

success: A claimed multi-writer adapter preserves both nonconflicting updates or rejects/retries a detectable conflict.
Same-key concurrent operation produces one semantic dispatch or an explicit conflict when that idempotency property is claimed.
failure: Both writes acknowledge yet one accepted update is overwritten under a claimed serializable multi-writer profile.
Same-key calls create two threads under a claimed concurrent duplicate-suppression property.
unsupported: An enforced and externally verified single-writer-only contract excludes the two-writer variant; mere comment or per-instance queue is not enforcement.
unknown: Cannot associate acknowledgments and recovered state with the same file incarnation.

cuts.baseline_static_prediction: The queue is per-instance. Duplicate-key check lies outside the queued mutation. These source-level schedules are possible unless a surrounding constraint excludes them; no runtime reproduction has occurred.

cuts.title: 意图已提交但消息尚未交给宿主
initial_state: A committed JSON version contains a relay ID M with sent=false and matching project state.
The destination is a worker in one variant and the lead in another; keep their recovery policies distinct.
cut_points: After Store intent commit but before Native.deliver
After recovery marks inactive worker interrupted, before any explicit resume
cuts.perturbation: Application process crash before delivery; stable intent preservation is a profile assumption, not inferred from Store acknowledgment.
observables: explicit user resume/retry request and any new generation/relay ID

success: Recovered committed intent is visible or its missing guarantee is explicitly reported.
An interrupted worker is not silently restarted; a hold is reported as hold, not as completed delivery.
New retry/generation retains a relation to the old unresolved attempt rather than treating old execution as impossible.
failure: Intent is silently dropped while its associated state is claimed committed under the same durability contract.
An unsent intent is reported as remote business success, or the documented recovery gate is bypassed.
unsupported: No durable storage profile exists to justify a recovery guarantee.
unknown: The submitter cannot establish whether pre-crash intent reached the committed storage version.

cuts.baseline_static_prediction: Workbench deliberately leaves inactive workers interrupted and does not promise unconditional automatic at-least-once redelivery. Native session creation before local association is an additional adjacent orphan seam, not simulated here.

cuts.title: live ID 早退绕过失败的目标耐久屏障
initial_state: Use a worker-report relay to the lead. The lead is not a thread target, so a failed delivery does not change its thread phase and same-ID retry_delivery remains reachable.
Target has an active routed JSONL write handle. M is not yet durably present; no model assumptions about business completion.
cut_points: followup publishes live inbox/session event M
Target drain fails before commit, or append rollback succeeds; buffered M is retained
User requests retry_delivery, clearing the outbox error
Native sees live M and returns before flush; outbox.sent marker commits
Process crashes before any later successful target drain
cuts.perturbation: Future model chooses explicit target-no-commit failure and forbids a later successful drain until the crash. A generic flush rejection is insufficient to choose this trace.
observables: lead relay M and retry_delivery request
target-specific drain/failure boundary or controlled synthetic write failure
whether any persistence barrier runs on the duplicate path
recovered target history and recovered outbox.sent

success: A durable-delivery implementation does not acknowledge the duplicate as durable until the old batch is proven committed or a new target barrier succeeds.
If it cannot do so, the result retains uncertainty and the intent remains recoverable.
failure: Under target-no-commit plus no-later-drain assumptions, sent=true survives while recovery lacks M, contradicting a claimed durable recipient-acceptance property.
unsupported: Target is a failed worker whose phase gate prevents same-M retry, rather than the specified lead path.
Actual backend has a different visibility/durability contract or no target-scoped fault/probe exists.
unknown: Flush failed only on another session, rollback outcome is ambiguous, or some later drain may have persisted M.

cuts.baseline_static_prediction: Fixed DSH separates live publication from durable drain and retains failed batches; Native's duplicate branch skips the barrier. This establishes the relevant code seam, not an observed lost-message incident.

cuts.title: 目标已保存而全局 flush 或 sent 标记失败
initial_state: Message M reaches the target's durable prefix.
The local outbox still has sent=false; external business effects have their own unknown/not-observed state.
cut_points: Variant A: target writer succeeds, another active writer fails, service-wide flush rejects
Variant B: service flush succeeds, Store.change for sent marker fails
Optional process crash after either failure and before durable reconciliation
cuts.perturbation: Future isolated fault profile injects a different-writer failure or local marker-write failure; target persistence remains independently observable.
observables: local marker write result and subsequent error-state write result
separate business target effect evidence if any

success: Failure is classified at its actual boundary; it is not proof target delivery failed.
Retry preserves M identity and checks recipient state; receipt is not promoted to task/business success.
failure: The system treats the exception as proof of no target acceptance and issues an unsafe new semantic action.
Local sent or accepted message alone is used as proof of business effect.
unsupported: No target-scoped observation or controlled unrelated-writer failure is available.
unknown: Global failure or local persistence failure lacks sufficient attribution; target result remains unknown rather than definitely absent.

cuts.baseline_static_prediction: The current Projects catch may report a not-delivered message even when the failed step is marker persistence or another session's flush. This is an interpretation boundary, not proof any duplicate business effect occurred.

cuts.title: 旧回执、撤权和仅恢复 snapshot
initial_state: A command Q has historical receipt R in a complete in-memory journal; a later distinct command revokes authorization or cancels the task.
Variant A restores a complete authenticated durable journal. Variant B has only a read snapshot; no durable adapter is assumed.
cut_points: After model apply returns R but before any adapter persistence
After current authorization changes, before exact Q redelivery
After restart with full journal versus an attempted snapshot-only restoration
cuts.perturbation: Future model varies whether the exact request identity and current grant state survive; no real commands are sent.
observables: outbound request count caused by duplicate response

success: Exact retry may return R unchanged without creating a new event, renewing authorization or sending another external request.
Different content with reused requestId is rejected.
Only a complete supported recovery path claims restored command deduplication; a read snapshot is not advertised as a durable kernel restore.
failure: Adapter treats old authorize/dispatch receipt as current permission or fresh send trigger.
Restart loses dedup identities but reuses stream identity while claiming exact retry safety.
In-memory apply success is called durable acknowledgment without an implemented persistence boundary.
unsupported: No durable Record adapter exists: persistence recovery is explicitly unsupported, as in S1.
unknown: Journal or current grant provenance cannot be authenticated/bounded, or receipt cannot be tied to its history incarnation.

cuts.baseline_static_prediction: Record intentionally returns historical receipts and does no I/O. The potential violation is an adapter's incorrect refinement, not the known-request branch itself.

not_claimed: absence of fsync proves historical data loss
